kq_binary_search.prompt: Binary search on a sorted array of n items. What's the time complexity?
kq_binary_search.green: O(log n). Each step halves the range.
kq_binary_search.yellow: Log-something? It halves stuff... O(log n), I think.
kq_binary_search.red: O(n). It checks every item, just faster.
kq_binary_search.ducky: O(log n). Each comparison halves what's left to search.

kq_nested_loops.prompt: A loop over n items inside another loop over n items. Complexity?
kq_nested_loops.green: O(n squared): n times n steps.
kq_nested_loops.red: O(2n). Two loops, so two n.
kq_nested_loops.ducky: O(n^2). Nested loops multiply; loops one after another add.

kq_hash_map.prompt: What's the average time to look up a key in a hash map?
kq_hash_map.green: O(1) on average; O(n) worst case with lots of collisions.
kq_hash_map.yellow: Fast? Constant... unless collisions. Probably O(1).
kq_hash_map.red: O(log n), because hash maps keep their keys sorted.
kq_hash_map.ducky: O(1) on average. Hash maps aren't sorted; heavy collisions can make it O(n).

kq_two_sum.prompt: Does any pair in an array add up to a target? What's the fast approach?
kq_two_sum.green: One pass with a hash set: check if target minus x was seen.
kq_two_sum.yellow: Maybe a set? Store what I've seen, then... check it?
kq_two_sum.red: Two nested loops. Brute force is honest work.
kq_two_sum.ducky: One pass plus a hash set is O(n). Nested loops work too, but they're O(n^2).

kq_recursion_base.prompt: A recursive function has no base case. What happens?
kq_recursion_base.green: It never stops calling itself: stack overflow.
kq_recursion_base.yellow: It loops forever? Something overflows. The stack?
kq_recursion_base.red: It returns zero. The compiler adds a base case.
kq_recursion_base.ducky: It recurses until the call stack overflows. Write the base case first.

kq_left_join.prompt: Users LEFT JOIN Orders. What do you get back?
kq_left_join.green: Every user, plus their orders; no orders means NULLs.
kq_left_join.yellow: All the users? And some orders? With blanks, maybe.
kq_left_join.red: Only the users who have orders.
kq_left_join.ducky: All left rows are kept; missing right-side values are NULL. INNER JOIN drops them.

kq_index_tradeoff.prompt: What's the main trade-off of adding a database index?
kq_index_tradeoff.green: Faster reads, but more storage and slower writes.
kq_index_tradeoff.yellow: Faster queries... and it costs something. Space?
kq_index_tradeoff.ducky: Indexes speed up lookups but use storage and slow down inserts and updates.

kq_http_403.prompt: You're logged in, but the admin page refuses you. Best HTTP status code?
kq_http_403.green: 403 Forbidden: we know who you are; you're not allowed.
kq_http_403.red: 500. The server is clearly upset with me.
kq_http_403.ducky: 403: logged in, not allowed. 401: not logged in. Some sites send 404 to hide that a page exists.

kq_idempotent.prompt: Name an idempotent HTTP method: sending it 5 times has the same effect as once.
kq_idempotent.green: PUT. Same request, same final state.
kq_idempotent.yellow: Not POST... GET-ish? PUT, I think.
kq_idempotent.red: POST. It posts the same thing every time.
kq_idempotent.ducky: PUT (also GET and DELETE). POST usually creates something new on each call.

kq_rebase_merge.prompt: Git: what's the difference between merge and rebase?
kq_rebase_merge.green: Merge adds a merge commit; rebase replays my commits on top.
kq_rebase_merge.yellow: Rebase is... cleaner? It moves the commits somewhere.
kq_rebase_merge.red: Rebase deletes the other branch. Merge is the free version.
kq_rebase_merge.ducky: Rebase rewrites your commits onto a new base. Never rebase commits others already pulled.

kq_testing_pyramid.prompt: In the testing pyramid, which tests should you have the most of?
kq_testing_pyramid.green: Unit tests: fast and cheap. Fewest end-to-end tests.
kq_testing_pyramid.yellow: The small ones? Unit tests. Mostly.
kq_testing_pyramid.red: End-to-end UI tests. Click everything, every time.
kq_testing_pyramid.ducky: Many unit tests, fewer integration tests, fewest slow end-to-end tests.

kq_race_condition.prompt: Two threads each add 1 to a counter 1,000 times. The result is 1,734. Why?
kq_race_condition.green: A race: read-modify-write isn't atomic. Use a lock.
kq_race_condition.yellow: The threads fight? Something about locks, maybe.
kq_race_condition.red: Integer overflow. The CPU got tired.
kq_race_condition.ducky: Unsynchronized updates overwrite each other. Use a lock or an atomic counter.

kq_deadlock.prompt: Thread A holds lock 1 and wants lock 2. Thread B holds 2 and wants 1. What is this?
kq_deadlock.green: A deadlock. Fix it by always taking locks in the same order.
kq_deadlock.yellow: They're stuck? A... deadlock. Yes. Deadlock.
kq_deadlock.red: A memory leak. Restart and pray.
kq_deadlock.ducky: A deadlock. A consistent lock order, or timeouts, prevents it.

kq_cache_first_fix.prompt: The same rarely-changing data is read 10,000 times a second. The DB is struggling. First fix?
kq_cache_first_fix.green: Put a cache with an expiry time in front of the database.
kq_cache_first_fix.yellow: Cache it? In memory, somewhere? Yes. Cache.
kq_cache_first_fix.red: Rewrite the app in a trendier language.
kq_cache_first_fix.ducky: Cache hot, rarely-changing reads with a time-to-live. Measure first, then optimize.

kq_load_balancer.prompt: What does a load balancer do?
kq_load_balancer.green: Spreads requests across servers and skips unhealthy ones.
kq_load_balancer.yellow: Balances... load. Across the servers. Evenly?
kq_load_balancer.ducky: It distributes traffic across servers and routes around the unhealthy ones.

kq_url_shortener.prompt: Design a URL shortener. What happens when someone opens a short link?
kq_url_shortener.green: Look up the code in a fast key-value store, then redirect.
kq_url_shortener.yellow: Find the long URL... and send them there? A redirect?
kq_url_shortener.red: Generate a brand-new short link every time.
kq_url_shortener.ducky: A cached key-value lookup, then an HTTP 301 or 302 redirect. Ask about scale first!

kq_sql_injection.prompt: What's the best defense against SQL injection?
kq_sql_injection.green: Parameterized queries. Never glue user input into SQL.
kq_sql_injection.yellow: Sanitize... stuff? Escape the quotes, I guess.
kq_sql_injection.red: Check the input in the browser. Done.
kq_sql_injection.ducky: Parameterized queries (prepared statements). Browser-side checks are easy to bypass.

kq_password_storage.prompt: How should an app store user passwords?
kq_password_storage.green: A salted hash with a slow algorithm made for passwords.
kq_password_storage.yellow: Encrypted? Hashed? Hashed. With salt, I think.
kq_password_storage.ducky: Slow, salted password hashing. If a site can email you your password, it's stored wrong.

kq_star_conflict.prompt: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a teammate.
kq_star_conflict.green: We tested both ideas, the data picked one, and I learned why.
kq_star_conflict.yellow: Um, once? We disagreed. Then we... agreed?
kq_star_conflict.red: I don't disagree. I'm always right.
kq_star_conflict.ducky: Use STAR: Situation, Task, Action, Result. No team yet? Use open source or clients.

kq_failure_story.prompt: Tell me about a project that failed.
kq_failure_story.green: It shipped late. I learned to cut scope early. Here's how.
kq_failure_story.yellow: Everything worked out in the end, honestly. Mostly.
kq_failure_story.red: Nothing I build fails. Some of it just never runs.
kq_failure_story.ducky: Pick a real failure, own your part, and show what you changed afterwards.

kq_learn_fast.prompt: How do you learn a new technology quickly?
kq_learn_fast.green: Build a tiny project, read the docs, ask for a review.
kq_learn_fast.yellow: Videos? Lots of videos. At 2x speed.
kq_learn_fast.red: I ask Guessomatic and paste whatever it says.
kq_learn_fast.ducky: A small project, the official docs, and feedback. Explain it back to check you get it.

kq_estimate.prompt: Your task will take twice as long as planned. What do you do?
kq_estimate.green: Tell my lead early, with options to cut scope or move dates.
kq_estimate.yellow: Tell my lead? Soon-ish? Maybe cut... something?
kq_estimate.red: Say it's 90% done. For three weeks.
kq_estimate.ducky: Flag slips early and bring options. Surprises are worse than bad news.
